data.name: Ishavari
data.gender_notes: Ishavari is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ishavari is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Ish’ meaning god and ‘Var’ meaning grace. This name signifies the embodiment of grace and divine blessings. In Hindu mythology, Ishavari is revered as the goddess of compassion and grace, who bestows her blessings upon her devotees. The name Ishavari carries the meaning “Goddess of grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ishavari usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ishavari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ishavari total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Ishavari is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture and represents the divine feminine. Devotees often invoke Goddess Ishavari to seek her blessings for prosperity, success, and happiness in their lives. This name holds a significant place in the Indian subcontinent, particularly in Nepal, where Goddess Ishavari is one of the eight forms of the goddess Durga. Cultural festivals and rituals dedicated to this goddess are widely observed in both Nepal and India.
data.spiritual_significance: Ishavari carries immense spiritual significance in Hinduism as the embodiment of grace and compassion. She is believed to grant her devotees the boon of purity of heart and the removal of miseries and sufferings. Worshiping Ishavari is considered to be a powerful way to seek forgiveness for sins, establish a spiritual link with the divine, and attain inner peace and tranquility. Moreover, this name has the ability to inspire and uplift one's soul, fostering a deep sense of love, devotion, and surrendering to the Almighty.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ishavari: Goddess of divine grace and supreme power, symbolizing the absolute surrender and trust in the divine will. She embodies the nurturing and protective aspect of the universe, providing strength and support in times of need.
